story.head: Kolesar meets his old team
paras: The Red Wings have won two in a row, while the Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Friday. Going in, the Golden Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Wings last in the Atlantic (tied for 16th).

The Golden Knights have played better than their record (.633) says: their chances are worth about .691, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Red Wings (.577 on chances worth .634), where their finishing has held them back.

The Golden Knights (1st) and the Red Wings (2nd) both draw more penalties than they take. The Golden Knights have had shaky goaltending (31st). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Red Wings’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. As for the Red Wings, they block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and have a dangerous power play (3rd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Mark Stone (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL. For the Red Wings, Alex DeBrincat (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with nine points in his last five games.

John Gibson (4-4-1 / .874 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Detroit. Vegas has two options in net: Adin Hill (5-2-0 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) and Carter Hart (4-3-1 / .889 SV% in 8 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Hill got the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Gibson has a .938 save percentage in six starts against the Golden Knights, well above his usual .896. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
